title: About this dashboard
text:
The West Boundary Water Security dashboard is a pilot tool developed to support the Regional District of Kootenay Boundary (RDKB) and the KRWAC Agriculture and Water Working Group in planning for agricultural water supply and storage in the West Boundary (Kettle River watershed, Midway and upstream).
Its purpose is to make public water information easy to see and understand, so that producers, First Nations, local government, provincial agencies, and other water users can share a common picture of seasonal conditions and drought risk.

title: About this dashboard
text:
Planning and engagement only
This dashboard is for planning and community engagement purposes only. It is not a regulatory or compliance monitoring tool. Live readings are provisional and unverified and should not be used for enforcement or for decisions that require official, quality-assured data.

title: About this dashboard
text:
Data sources

Streamflow — Environment and Climate Change Canada (ECCC) real-time hydrometric service and the Water Survey of Canada HYDAT historical database, accessed with the open-source tidyhydat R package.
Groundwater — B.C. Provincial Groundwater Observation Well Network (PGOWN).
All data are public and provided under open licences (including the Open Government Licence – British Columbia).

title: About this dashboard
text:
Privacy and responsible use
The dashboard uses public and voluntarily shared information only. If producer-contributed inputs are added in future (for example well levels, repeat photo points, or irrigation timing), they would be aggregated or anonymised so that individual operations cannot be identified, consistent with FOIPPA and with the project’s commitment to a transparent, non-regulatory process.

title: About this dashboard
text:
Ownership and upkeep
The dashboard is built entirely with open-source tools (Quarto + R) so it can be fully owned, hosted, and maintained by the Regional District. Source files, data-build scripts, and documentation are included in the project repository, and the historical baselines can be refreshed with a single command.

title: West Boundary Water Security
text:
This site is a pilot dashboard supporting agricultural water supply and storage planning in the RDKB West Boundary — the Kettle River watershed from Midway upstream (Electoral Area E), including the communities of Baldy, Beaverdell, Bridesville, Midway, and Rock Creek.
It brings public water information together in one accessible place to help producers, First Nations, local government, and agencies share a common picture of seasonal water conditions and drought risk. It is intended for planning and engagement only — not for regulatory monitoring.

title: West Boundary Water Security
text:
Open the dashboard
→ West Boundary Water Security dashboard
The dashboard includes:

Current conditions — live flow status for each monitoring station, scored against decades of record, with a project-area map of stations and communities.
Seasonal & drought risk — this year’s streamflow compared to the historical normal range, monthly climatology, and per-site comparisons.
Snowpack & water supply — Grano Creek snow water equivalent as a leading indicator for summer supply.
Groundwater & aquifers — water-table levels at Kettle valley observation wells (Grand Forks, Beaverdell, Midway) versus their historical norms.
Stations & live data — the underlying monitoring network and live records.

title: West Boundary Water Security
text:
How it works
The dashboard combines live readings with decades of historical record to show whether the watershed is tracking wetter or drier than normal for the time of year. All information is public and openly licensed, and the whole tool is built with open-source software so it can be fully owned and maintained by the Regional District. See the About page for data sources and responsible-use notes.
